plan.estimand: omnibus F-statistic difference in population means across 3 independent groups
plan.hypothesis: H₀: μ₁ = μ₂ = μ₃ vs. H₁: at least one mean differs
assumptions: Observations within each group are independent and identically normally distributed
Homogeneity of variance: common population variance σ² across all groups
Fixed effects model: groups are of primary interest (not random sample from population of groups)
Population eta-squared η² = 0.06 represents the true effect size under the alternative hypothesis
scientific_notes: Eta-squared (η²) quantifies proportion of variance in the outcome explained by group membership
Relationship to non-centrality: η² relates to the ANOVA effect size through λ = n·k·η²/(1-η²), where n is per-group sample size and k is number of groups
F-distribution under alternative hypothesis is non-central with df1 = k-1 = 2, df2 = N-k, non-centrality parameter λ
This is a fixed-effects omnibus test at the 0.05 significance level; power calculation assumes effect size is specified under the alternative

answer.summary: For a balanced one-way fixed effects ANOVA with 3 independent groups, common variance, and population eta-squared η² = 0.06, the minimum integer sample size per group yielding at least 80% power at α = 0.05 for the omnibus F test is 52 participants per group. This achieves 80.56% power and requires a total of 156 participants (52 per group × 3 groups). The preceding design (n = 51) yields 79.73% power, confirming that 52 is the smallest admissible integer design meeting the 80% power target.
answer.method: one_way_anova – Power analysis via non-central F distribution using pwr::pwr.anova.test(). Eta-squared η² = 0.06 converted to Cohen's f = √(0.06/0.94) ≈ 0.2526. Sample size inverted to target power 0.80 at α = 0.05 with k = 3 groups, yielding continuous solution n ≈ 51.33 participants per group. Integer rounding ceiling(51.33) = 52 participants per group. Power verified at integer designs: n = 52 achieves 0.8056 power; n = 51 achieves 0.7973 power.
assumptions: Observations within each group are independent and identically normally distributed with a common population variance σ²
Fixed effects model: the 3 groups are of primary interest (not a random sample from a larger population of groups)
Population eta-squared η² = 0.06 represents the true effect size under the alternative hypothesis H₁
Balanced design: equal sample size per group
Omnibus F test: H₀: μ₁ = μ₂ = μ₃ vs. H₁: at least one mean differs
limitations: Sample size calculation assumes the population effect size η² = 0.06 is known and fixed; actual power depends on the true effect size
Calculation applies to the omnibus F test only; if follow-up pairwise comparisons are planned, additional multiplicity adjustment (e.g., Bonferroni) may reduce power
Non-centrality parameter and power assume normality and homogeneity of variance; sensitivity to violations is not assessed
Design is balanced; unequal group sizes would require recalculation

executions.code:
# Load required package
library(pwr)

# Define parameters
k <- 3                    # number of groups
eta_squared <- 0.06       # population eta-squared
alpha <- 0.05             # significance level
target_power <- 0.8       # target power

# Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f effect size
# Relationship: f = sqrt(eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared))
f_effect <- sqrt(eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared))

cat("Effect size parameters:\n")
cat("  Eta-squared (η²):", eta_squared, "\n")
cat("  Cohen's f:", f_effect, "\n\n")

# Calculate sample size per group using pwr.anova.test()
# This returns the per-group sample size for a balanced design
result <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  f = f_effect,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power
)

cat("Power analysis result:\n")
cat("  Number of groups (k):", result$k, "\n")
cat("  Cohen's f:", result$f, "\n")
cat("  Significance level (α):", result$sig.level, "\n")
cat("  Target power:", result$power, "\n")
cat("  Sample size per group (continuous):", result$n, "\n\n")

# Round up to nearest integer (standard practice)
n_integer <- ceiling(result$n)
cat("Minimum integer sample size per group:", n_integer, "\n\n")

# Verify power at the rounded sample size
verified_power <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  f = f_effect,
  sig.level = alpha,
  n = n_integer
)

cat("Verified power at n =", n_integer, "per group:", verified_power$power, "\n\n")

# Also check power at n-1 to confirm n_integer is the minimum
power_at_prev <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  f = f_effect,
  sig.level = alpha,
  n = n_integer - 1
)

cat("Power at n =", n_integer - 1, "per group:", power_at_prev$power, "\n\n")

# Calculate total sample size
N_total <- k * n_integer
cat("Total sample size (across all groups):", N_total, "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom (between groups):", k - 1, "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom (within groups):", N_total - k, "\n\n")

# Compute non-centrality parameter for verification
ncp <- sqrt(n_integer * k * f_effect^2)
cat("Non-centrality parameter (λ):", ncp, "\n")

# Critical F value
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1 = k - 1, df2 = N_total - k)
cat("Critical F value at α = 0.05:", f_crit, "\n")

# Return results
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_integer, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(verified_power$power, 4), unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "power_at_preceding_design", value = round(power_at_prev$power, 4), unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "total_sample_size", value = N_total, unit = "participants"),
    list(metric = "cohens_f", value = round(f_effect, 4), unit = "effect_size")
  )
)

cat("\n=== FINAL RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Minimum sample size per group (n):", n_integer, "participants_per_group\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", n_integer, ":", round(verified_power$power, 4), "\n")
cat("Power at n =", n_integer - 1, ":", round(power_at_prev$power, 4), "\n")

jsonlite::toJSON(POWER_AGENT_RESULT, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15)

# Evidence e2; success=true

# Load required package
library(pwr)

# Define parameters
k <- 3                    # number of groups
eta_squared <- 0.06       # population eta-squared
alpha <- 0.05             # significance level
target_power <- 0.8       # target power

# Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f effect size
# Relationship: f = sqrt(eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared))
f_effect <- sqrt(eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared))

# Calculate sample size per group using pwr.anova.test()
result <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  f = f_effect,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power
)

# Round up to nearest integer (standard practice)
n_integer <- ceiling(result$n)

# Verify power at the rounded sample size
verified_power <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  f = f_effect,
  sig.level = alpha,
  n = n_integer
)

# Check power at n-1 to confirm n_integer is the minimum
power_at_prev <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  f = f_effect,
  sig.level = alpha,
  n = n_integer - 1
)

# Calculate total sample size
N_total <- k * n_integer

# Emit results
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_integer, unit = "participants_per_group"),
      list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(verified_power$power, 4), unit = "probability"),
      list(metric = "power_at_preceding_design", value = round(power_at_prev$power, 4), unit = "probability"),
      list(metric = "total_sample_size", value = N_total, unit = "participants"),
      list(metric = "cohens_f", value = round(f_effect, 4), unit = "effect_size")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(POWER_AGENT_RESULT)
